items.title: How it works
items.text:
• Upvote: open an idea's discussion and click the Upvote button (the ▲ in the bottom-left corner of the discussion's opening post). The upvote tally drives the ordering above. GitHub Discussions support upvotes only — there is no downvote. Add a comment with your use case for extra signal.
  • Propose a new idea: open a discussion in the Ideas category. If the maintainers authorize it (by adding the roadmap authorized label), it appears in the table automatically.
  • Follow progress: an idea's status is updated as it moves toward implementation; the linked discussion carries the detailed conversation.

Feedback and feature requests are always welcome via the GitHub issue tracker as well.

items.title: Versioning & Releases
items.text: How the ClinVar-GKM bundle schema and its data releases are versioned, how breaking changes roll out, and how to stay informed.

items.title: Two things are versioned
items.text:
• The schema — the shape of the bundle (its fields, types, and references). It carries a semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
  • The data releases — the periodic bundles themselves: a monthly full, weekly fulls and weekly deltas, each dated. Every release conforms to a specific schema version.

items.title: What the schema version means
items.text:
Change Version bump Where it is published What it means for you MAJOR (2.0.0) Breaking A new line folder, v2/2.0/ A bundle valid under the old version may no longer validate or parse the same way — a field was removed, renamed, retyped, restructured, or made required. You may need to update your code. MINOR (1.2.0) Additive, or a correction that rewrites published bundles A new line folder, v1/1.2/ New optional fields, sections or values, or corrected content in republished bundles. Old consumers keep working unchanged. PATCH (1.1.1) Cosmetic The current line folder No change to valid instances, and no published file is rewritten — only new dated files are added.

A change to a string value's format that leaves the schema shape untouched (same fields and types) is not a schema version change — it is recorded in the Changelog. A content-only correction that must rewrite published bundles is still released as a new MINOR line, even when the schema shape is unchanged. The new line's schema $id version and every bundle's schema_version move to that MINOR too, so a bundle's schema_version always names the line folder it was published in. A PATCH never rewrites a published file.

Upstream standards are insulated

ClinVar-GKM builds on the GA4GH GKM schemas (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec). When one of those bumps, the ClinVar-GKM version changes only by the actual effect on the bundle we emit — not automatically. An upstream major release that doesn't change any field we emit is not a major change for ClinVar-GKM.

items.title: 1.1.0 and general availability
items.text:
1.1.0 is generally available (GA). It was a breaking change — the proposition sections were renamed — released as a MINOR under the initial-stabilization exception (ADR 0006). It was published into a new line folder, v1/1.1/, and the 1.0.1 generation became the frozen line v1/1.0/ (ADR 0009). The stabilization period ends with 1.1.0:

  • Published files are immutable. The bytes behind a published monthly or delta are never replaced. A rollover can move a file to a new folder without changing its name, bytes or checksum. Weekly full bundles are the one exception: they are deleted after their month, and any past week can be rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas. The index.json files, feed.xml and every 00-latest path are pointers that move with each release.
  • Every later breaking change opens a new MAJOR line (v2/2.0/), with the RFC process below.

See the 1.1.0 changelog for the migration notes.

items.title: How breaking changes roll out
items.text:
A breaking (MAJOR) change opens a new line folder, v2/2.0/, built in full — every monthly full and delta in the published window — alongside v1/. At the switch-over:

  • The prior line is frozen: it gets no new releases, and its files stay downloadable and unchanged.
  • A frozen line is kept indefinitely. There is no end-of-life date, no deprecated status and no deletion window.
  • The root manifest and the line's own index.json mark it "status": "frozen" with "superseded_by" naming the line that replaced it, and the frozen folder carries a MANIFEST.json (size and sha256 per file) and a README.txt saying what replaced it and why.

Only one line is current at a time; frozen lines accumulate. A new MINOR line (for example v1/1.2/) freezes the line it replaces in the same way.

The published schema always matches the data

The schema in schema/clinvar-gkm/ is the source of truth and is updated in the same change as any adjustment to the emitted bundle — so a given release's data always validates against its stated schema version, and the published examples are validated against it.

items.title: Finding and pinning a version
items.text:
Each version line lives in its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/ (v1/1.1/, later v2/2.0/), with its own index.json. PATCH releases add new dated files to their line's folder; a new MINOR or MAJOR starts a new folder, and the line it replaces is frozen and kept indefinitely, its files unchanged (the 1.0.1 generation is the frozen line v1/1.0/). Inside a line the layout mirrors NCBI's ClinVar FTP site; see Downloads. A small root manifest at the bucket root, index.json, lists every line, its status and schema version, and where its own index.json and feed are. Its shape, as published for 1.1.0:

{
  "manifest_version": 2,
  "updated_at": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z",
  "base_url": "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org",
  "current": "v1/1.1",
  "versions": {
    "1.1": {"line": "v1/1.1", "major": 1, "minor": 1, "status": "current", "schema": "1.1.0",
            "superseded_by": null, "index": "v1/1.1/index.json", "feed": "v1/1.1/feed.xml"},
    "1.0": {"line": "v1/1.0", "major": 1, "minor": 0, "status": "frozen", "schema": "1.0.1",
            "superseded_by": "v1/1.1", "index": "v1/1.0/index.json", "feed": "v1/1.0/feed.xml"}
  }
}

versions is keyed by {major}.{minor}; paths are relative to base_url. A line is current or frozen; there is no eol field.

To pin to a line, read releases from that line's index.json and ignore the others. To track the latest, follow the line whose status is current. Every bundle also carries a top-level schema_version field, so you can confirm a file's exact version from the file itself.

items.title: Release notes
items.text:
• The Changelog records every schema change (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH) and every data re-release, with dates and migration pointers.
  • Each tagged release is listed on GitHub Releases with its source.
  • Each weekly delta's manifest gives its per-section added, updated and deleted counts; see Weekly Deltas.

items.title: Stay informed & have a say
items.text:
Subscribe

  • Watch the GitHub repository (Custom → Releases & Discussions) for release announcements and change proposals.
  • Subscribe to the release feed (Atom, each line's feed.xml, e.g. https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/feed.xml) in any feed reader.
  • Join the email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org, a Google Group for release announcements, change notices and RFCs about the repository, the data releases, tools and documentation. No GitHub account needed; see Stay Informed for how to join.

Before any breaking change, we open a Request for Comment (RFC) — a proposal with its rationale and migration impact — send subscribers an advance notice, and hold a minimum 4-week comment window so affected consumers can weigh in before the change is finalized. Every republish into a new line and every switch-over is announced in advance.

The decision records are ADR 0004 (schema versioning and release management), ADR 0006 (1.1.0 under the stabilization exception), and ADR 0008 (bundles are the public record) and ADR 0009 (R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar), proposed in PR #168.

items.title: ClinVar-GKM Primer
items.text:
Presented at GA4GH Connect — October 2, 2026

This primer was prepared for GA4GH Connect (October 2, 2026) to introduce ClinVar-GKM to the GKS community.

Download URLs predate 1.1.0

The download URLs and the per-release Parquet in this deck's Downloads slide predate 1.1.0. See Downloads for the current layout and the Changelog for what changed.

A ~8-minute (15-slide) introduction to ClinVar-GKM for a technical audience that knows ClinVar but is new to VA-Spec and the GKM model. It covers how ClinVar's complete data is organized today (shown with the real VCV XML schema), how the newest GKM standards (VRS 2.1.1 · Cat-VRS 1.1.1 · VA-Spec 1.1.0, on GKM-Core 1.3.0) reorganize it for consistent, accurate access, the bundle shape and class inventory, a worked example, the community profiles and ClinVar-specific implementer profiles in play, downloads, the transparency of how the data is produced, and who is adopting it for production.

items.text:
1. The starting point — ClinVar's complete truth is the weekly XML
  2. Anatomy of the XML — what "just extract the SCVs" really takes (real VCV schema)
  3. What it is — every ClinVar release rebuilt as one GKM bundle
  4. The GKM stack — VRS 2.1.1 · Cat-VRS 1.1.1 · VA-Spec 1.1.0 · GKM-Core 1.3.0 (all newly released)
  5. ClinVar → statements — SCV / VCV / RCV as VA-Spec Statements
  6. The GKM Bundle — compaction via ids + #/section/id pointers (like foreign keys); schema-driven Starter Kit / Toolkit
  7. Class inventory — the GKM classes in play (MappableConcept, ConceptSet, CategoricalVariant, Allele, CNV Count/Change, Statement, Proposition, EvidenceLine)
  8. Worked example — clinvar:10 (HFE p.His63Asp), statement → proposition → variant → VRS
  9. Profiles & recipes — Cat-VRS recipes and VA-Spec community profiles
  10. Implementer profiles — custom propositions + ClinVar-specific extensions
  11. Downloads — monthly full + weekly deltas, JSON & Parquet
  12. Transparency — how every value is produced and verified
  13. Momentum — groups adopting it for production
